correctness.rationale: Direct finite Birkhoff downset implication derives the pair normal form (K,L) and exact intrinsic join; the distributive law is equivalent to the monotone map D preserving binary unions, with an explicit three-element witness for failure. For q external to ↑I, D(K) iff some predecessor support S_p is contained in K; union preservation holds iff each minimal support is principal. Nondistributivity forces an induced four-point three-minimum star, hence at least nine downsets; restriction is noninjective if P has another point. The explicit nine-element witness and its three possible antecedents achieve the bound. An independently written direct implication/distributivity program tested every naturally labeled poset of sizes 1–5, and support equivalences for all 5,231 posets of sizes 1–6. Finite checks corroborate but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The result answers a qualitative structural question raised by a natural logical identity: when a materializer, known to be meet closed but not always ambient-join closed, has a distributive inherited-order lattice. The exact minimal-support criterion applies to every antecedent and gives a polynomial-time decision method; the sharp unique nine-element obstruction identifies the first algebra size at which this lattice can be intrinsically nondistributive. A full structural classification has independent mathematical use beyond the known single example.
